title: Determination is recorded
description: A hearing determination (upheld / dismissed / reduced) must be recorded on the Citation before the citation-lifecycle may advance to adjudicated, and it writes a CaseEvents entry.
name: tt-determination-01

title: Dismissal reverses consequences
description: When a determination dismisses a Citation, any assessed license points are reversed and any paid amount is refunded, restoring the Driver to make-whole state.
name: tt-determination-02

title: Lifecycle transitions are guarded
description: Every state transition is gated by its guard condition and the firing role; the state-machine backbone rejects illegal transitions and logs each accepted one to CaseEvents.
name: tt-state-01

title: Citation requires driver, violation and jurisdiction
description: A citation must reference exactly one driver, one violation type, and one issuing jurisdiction.
name: r1

title: Citation status is computed, never stored
description: CitationStatus is re-derived on every read from raw facts and child events; there is no stored status column to drift.
name: r10

title: No response by deadline is a default judgment
description: If the response window passes with no RespondedOn, the citation moves to Adjudicated by default.
name: r11

title: Contest status follows the latest hearing
description: ContestStatus is derived from the newest related hearing: NotContested | HearingRequested → Scheduled → Heard.
name: r12

title: Only a manager schedules a hearing
description: Transitioning a hearing from HearingRequested to Scheduled is a manager-role action.
name: r13

title: Response due date is derived from the jurisdiction
description: ResponseDueDate = IssuedOn + the issuing jurisdiction's DaysToRespond. Changing the jurisdiction's rule re-derives every citation under it.
name: r2

title: Fine is the violation's base fine
description: The amount owed starts at the violation type's BaseFineUsd for the citation's jurisdiction.
name: r20

title: Late payment incurs a jurisdiction penalty
description: If payment is not made by the pay-by date, a penalty of LatePenaltyPct of the fine is added.
name: r21

title: Prolonged non-payment goes to collections
description: A Late citation becomes Collections after DaysLateToCollections days past the pay-by date.
name: r22

title: A dismissed citation owes nothing
description: If a hearing dismisses the citation, PaymentStatus is NotOwed regardless of the fine.
name: r23

title: A response is pay or contest
description: Responding means either paying the fine or requesting a hearing; either sets RespondedOn and advances the citation to Responded.
name: r3

title: Active points roll up to the driver
description: A driver's ActivePoints is the sum of points from adjudicated, non-dismissed citations.
name: r30

title: Points drive license warning then suspension
description: LicenseStatus is Warning at the jurisdiction's PointWarningThreshold and Suspended at PointSuspensionThreshold.
name: r31

title: Regulations are data, not code
description: Every regulatory knob — deadlines, fines, penalties, thresholds, school caps — is a column on Jurisdictions, editable without code changes.
name: r40

title: Overdue work is urgent
description: A work-queue item whose due date is in the past is urgent and sorts to the top.
name: r50

title: Work items mirror their subject's deadline
description: A work item's DueDate is carried from its subject (e.g. Citations.ResponseDueDate or PaymentDueDate).
name: r51

title: Overrides require a reason
description: Any OVERRIDE audit entry must carry a non-empty Reason; the trail is append-only.
name: r60

title: Every assistant turn is costed
description: Each assistant turn records input/output tokens and the exact pricing version used, so TotalCost is fully derivable.
name: r70

title: Assistant answers are grounded in live data
description: The assistant answers about a citation/rule/portal from live vw_* reads and the rulebook, recording each exchange as an AssistantTurns row.
name: tt-assistant-01

title: Every turn is cost-accounted
description: Each AssistantTurns row records input/output tokens and a computed cost via ModelPricingVersions for the turn's AiModel.
name: tt-assistant-02

title: Every state-affecting change is logged
description: Each status change, override, payment, and edit writes an append-only AuditLogEntries (and where lifecycle-relevant, a CaseEvents) row.
name: tt-audit-01

title: The log never contradicts the derived state
description: The append-only history explains how current computed state was reached; it is additive narration, never an alternate source of truth.
name: tt-audit-02

title: Identity is resolved per request from the magic-link session
description: Each request resolves to an AppUsers row and role via the MagicLinkConfig flow; identity feeds every RBAC and scoping decision.
name: tt-auth-01

title: Citation status is derived, never stored
description: CitationStatus (Issued -> Responded -> InContest -> Adjudicated -> Closed) is computed on read from facts and child CaseEvents; no stored status column is authoritative.
name: tt-citation-01

title: Status order is monotonic
description: A citation may only advance forward through its lifecycle states; backward transitions require an explicit, logged override.
name: tt-citation-02

title: Contesting requires a timely contest response
description: The contest track only opens when DriverResponse = contest was recorded before the ResponseDeadline.
name: tt-contest-01

title: Contest track derives from the latest hearing
description: ContestStatus (NotContested | HearingRequested -> Scheduled -> Heard) is derived from the most recent Hearings row for the citation.
name: tt-contest-02

title: Determination decides liability
description: A hearing outcome of dismissed sets liability to none and zero fine owed; upheld confirms the original fine and points.
name: tt-contest-03

title: Response deadline derives from jurisdiction DaysToRespond
description: ResponseDeadline = IssueDate + the issuing jurisdiction's DaysToRespond; it recomputes whenever the rule changes.
name: tt-deadline-01

title: Base fine comes from the violation and jurisdiction
description: The base fine is the ViolationType base amount adjusted by the jurisdiction's fee schedule; it is data, not a constant.
name: tt-fee-01

title: Domain terms are defined as data
description: Every domain term used in a feature or rule is defined in GlossaryTerms under a GlossaryCategories group.
name: tt-glossary-01

title: Hearing requires a requested contest
description: A Hearings row may only be created for a citation whose ContestStatus is HearingRequested or later.
name: tt-hearing-01

title: Scheduling is manager-or-admin only
description: Only manager or admin roles may set a hearing's ScheduledDate; representatives request, they do not schedule.
name: tt-hearing-02

title: Citation requires driver, violation, jurisdiction
description: A citation must reference exactly one Driver, one ViolationType, and one issuing Jurisdiction; none may be null at intake.
name: tt-intake-01

title: Issue date present and not future-dated
description: Every citation records an IssueDate that is on or before today; a future issue date is rejected at intake.
name: tt-intake-02

title: Driver response is pay-or-contest before the deadline
description: The driver's response is one of {pay, contest} and must be recorded on or before the computed ResponseDeadline.
name: tt-intake-03

title: Active points roll up across a driver's citations
description: A driver's ActivePoints is the sum of points from non-dismissed, non-expired citations under each jurisdiction's point window.
name: tt-license-01

title: License track follows jurisdiction thresholds
description: LicenseStatus (Valid -> Warning -> Suspended) is derived by comparing ActivePoints against the jurisdiction's warning and suspension thresholds.
name: tt-license-02

title: Surfaces are gated by license/active flags
description: Packages, features, tables, and routes carry IsLicensed/IsActive flags; unlicensed surfaces are revealed as upgrade prompts, not deleted.
name: tt-license-pkg-01

title: Navigation is derived from PlatformNaviation rows
description: The sidebar and route tree render from PlatformNaviation filtered by the current role's RoleVisibility; there is no hand-maintained menu.
name: tt-nav-01

title: Route order and pinning are data
description: NavLevel, SortOrder, and PinToTop on PlatformNaviation determine ordering and which screens float to the top.
name: tt-nav-02

title: Payment track derives from payments and pay-by date
description: PaymentStatus (Pending -> Due -> Late -> Collections | Paid | NotOwed) is computed from Payments rows and the jurisdiction pay-by date.
name: tt-payment-01

title: Late penalty applies after the pay-by date
description: Once the pay-by date passes with no full payment, the jurisdiction's LatePenaltyPercent is added to AmountOwed.
name: tt-payment-02

title: Paid in full closes the case
description: When recorded Payments equal AmountOwed, PaymentStatus becomes Paid and the citation advances toward Closed.
name: tt-payment-03

title: The rulebook JSON is the single source of truth
description: All substrates (Postgres, Python, explain-dag, rulespeak) are mechanically derived from the rulebook by effortless build; edits go to the rulebook.
name: tt-platform-01

title: The platform describes itself
description: ERBTables/ERBFields/ERBFeatures/ERBPackages catalog every table, field, capability, and package so the app can render its own model.
name: tt-platform-02

title: Build is generate + load; drift is guarded
description: effortless build regenerates DDL/views/inserts and reloads the DB; a drift guard warns before a rebuild would clobber un-saved DB edits.
name: tt-platform-03

title: Work queue is computed from deadlines and status
description: WorkQueueItems are derived from overdue responses, due/late payments, and upcoming hearings, bucketed by urgency; nothing is hand-enqueued.
name: tt-queue-01

title: Four canonical roles govern access
description: Exactly four roles exist (admin, manager, representative, external-llm) and every permission decision references one of them.
name: tt-rbac-01

title: CRUD is per role, per table, per field
description: What each role may create/read/update/delete is data at the table and field grain; the enforced API consults it on every operation.
name: tt-rbac-02

title: Row access follows per-role WHERE policies
description: Each role-table pair carries a WHERE policy; a representative sees only their own citations while admin sees all, enforced on every vw_* read.
name: tt-rbac-03

title: Lower-trust roles get redacted projections
description: Fields denied to a role (e.g. PII for external-llm) are stripped from responses at projection time, not nulled afterward.
name: tt-rbac-04

title: Jurisdiction knobs are editable data
description: Deadlines, fines, penalty percentages, and point thresholds live in Jurisdictions/JurisdictionRules and every dependent value re-derives on edit.
name: tt-rules-01

title: Each jurisdiction rule cites its source
description: A JurisdictionRules row links to the JurisdictionSourceDocuments / ReferenceDocuments authority that justifies it.
name: tt-rules-02
